races.title: State Assembly, District 58
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Clarissa Cervantes
cands.bio: Riverside City Councilmember for Ward 2 since July 2021, the first woman to hold the seat. Former legislative field representative to Councilmember Andy Melendrez. Holds a master's degree in urban and regional planning. Ran for Assembly District 58 in 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party and California Federation of Labor Unions (2026 general election)
California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association and National Union of Healthcare Workers (2026)
California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Courage California and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund (2026)

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she moved to California. We found no statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion or school choice. Her campaign site makes claims about her council record, such as affordable housing votes and opposing utility rate increases, but names no specific votes or dates, so we could not confirm them. Her Ballotpedia page shows no candidate survey responses. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties. Details of her business career are not described anywhere we looked.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Riverside City Council Ward 2 member since July 2021; earlier a legislative field representative to a Riverside councilmember; chaired a Riverside Transit Agency advisory chapter; holds a master's in urban and regional planning; says she is a businesswoman.
qual.why: Local elected office, staff work for a legislator and a planning and policy degree fit the middle band. She has no state legislative service, and her business work is not described in any detail.
qual.label: Local elected office, staff work for a legislator and a planning and policy degree fit the middle band. She has no state legislative service, and her business work is not described in any detail.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says she has stood up to warehouse developers and fought irresponsible overdevelopment on the Riverside City Council, and that she championed environmental and open space protections. These are campaign claims, and no specific vote is cited.

back-police-order.evidence: Says that on the City Council she ensured police and firefighters had the staffing and resources to respond to emergencies. This is a campaign claim, and no specific vote is cited.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site says she has stood up to powerful developers by fighting irresponsible overdevelopment, specifically warehouse development that increases traffic and pollutes the air. It also says she voted to expand access to affordable housing and wants to cut red tape to build more affordable homes.

cands.name: Leticia Castillo
cands.bio: Republican Assemblymember for District 58 (Riverside and San Bernardino counties) since December 2024. Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist and Professional Clinical Counselor. Former clinician with Riverside County Department of Mental Health, now runs a private practice. Lost the 2022 primary, won the 2024 open seat.

endorsements.text: 2026: Republican Party of California, California Professional Firefighters, and Reform California, among others listed by Ballotpedia.

2024: Riverside Sheriff's Association, The Press-Enterprise, Rep. Ken Calvert and the Republican Party of California. Her own 2024 survey also lists Sheriff Chad Bianco, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and CRPA-PAC.

cands.gaps: We found no stated or documented position from Castillo on data centers, foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, or refusing big-donor money. We could not confirm which of her sponsored bills were passed, signed or defeated, or the bill numbers. The news articles about her voter ID push were only headlines on her campaign site, so we did not rely on them. Her campaign survey answers are her own statements, not records of what she did. We found no foreign ties and no documented controversies about her.

local.label: Roots 100: She was born in Riverside, calls herself a native of the Home Gardens-Corona area, and graduated from a local high school and a Corona cosmetology school in 1989.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Sitting Assemblymember since December 2024; owns a private psychotherapy practice; formerly a licensed clinical psychotherapist with the County of Riverside Department of Mental Health.
qual.why: She has held a legislative office for about one term and has run a small business, but she has no budget or policy career and a short legislative record. That puts her in the upper-middle range.
qual.label: She has held a legislative office for about one term and has run a small business, but she has no budget or policy career and a short legislative record. That puts her in the upper-middle range.

pro-life.evidence: Introduced a bill in February 2025 to promote adoption as an alternative to abortion, supported by the anti-abortion California Family Council.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site lists "Protect Second Amendment Rights" and says she is pro-Second Amendment and believes Californians have a right to protect and defend themselves.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site describes her as pro-school choice and lists "Ensure Quality Education" among her values. It gives no position on teacher pay.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site lists "Protect Prop 13" and "Lower Taxes" among her values. It does not call for eliminating homestead taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she would repeal Proposition 47, restore significant criminal penalties for organized retail theft, and require mandatory treatment for mentally ill and drug-addicted homeless people.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she supports reforming costly regulations like CEQA that make housing less affordable.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 6 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: She was born in Riverside, calls herself a native of the Home Gardens-Corona area, and graduated from a local high school and a Corona cosmetology school in 1989.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Said in her 2024 Ballotpedia candidate survey that it is crucial to reform costly government regulations like CEQA that make housing less affordable.
